headline: REUTERS EXCLUSIVE: Barrick Mining Eyes $30B London Tie-Up With Endeavour to Spin Off All African Assets
snippet: Barrick Mining is in early discussions to merge its African portfolio—spanning Tanzania, Zambia, DRC, and Ivory Coast—with Endeavour Mining in an all-share deal that could create a $30 billion London-listed gold major. The tie-up would be a merger of equals with little or no premium; Barrick is separately targeting a New York-listed North American spinoff (Nevada + Dominican Republic) by end-2026.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,514 as Silver Claws Back to $76 After May Selloff; Iran Tensions Fuel Safe-Haven Bid
snippet: Gold traded at $4,514/oz on June 2, up $54 from the prior session and $1,158 above year-ago levels, as renewed Iran-US tensions and roughly 50% market odds of a Fed rate hike before year-end supported safe-haven demand. Silver—which peaked near $89 in mid-May—has corrected to $76, still well above its 2025 lows and entering a sixth consecutive global supply deficit year.

headline: AYA SILVER HITS 5,100 g/t Over 2m at Morocco's Zgounder — Company's Richest Intercept on Record
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSXV: AYA) released hole ZG-RC-26-946 from the Zgounder Silver Mine in Morocco, returning 1,867 g/t Ag over 6.0m including 5,100 g/t over 2.0m—the highest-grade intercept in the company's history. A second hole returned 739 g/t Ag over 10.0m. Aya has drilled 9,250m (30.8%) of its 2026 exploration program to date with two rigs operating and additional rigs in transit.

headline: ORLA MINING SHARES -8%: Illegal Blockade Halts Camino Rojo as Workers Reject Mexico Profit-Sharing Payment
snippet: Orla Mining (TSX: OLA) reported an illegal work stoppage and physical blockade at its Camino Rojo gold mine in Zacatecas, Mexico, after unionized workers rejected the company's PTU (Mexican profit-sharing) payment. All production is halted with a federal labour conciliation meeting scheduled for June 2. Orla says it successfully settled a separate productivity bonus dispute prior to the blockade.

headline: IAMGOLD Lifts Côté Gold M&I Resource 12% to 20.3M oz — Gosselin Zone Fully Folded In for First Time
snippet: IAMGOLD (TSX: IMG) published an updated Mineral Resource estimate for Côté Gold in Ontario, adding 2.2 million oz to reach 20.3 million oz (M&I) after integrating the adjacent Gosselin zone into a single geological model for the first time. The estimate, effective March 31, 2026, sets the stage for a Q4 2026 mine expansion technical study and updated mine plan.

headline: PAN AMERICAN SILVER Approves $146M Timmins Expansion to Deepen Bell Creek and Access Vogel, Samson Deposits
snippet: Pan American Silver's (TSX: PAAS) board approved Phase 1 of a C$201 million ($146M) Timmins Camp expansion in Ontario: a 625m Bell Creek shaft deepening plus twin drifts targeting the Vogel and Samson satellite deposits. The company plans 118,000m of camp-wide drilling in 2026 aimed at resource conversion and mine-life extension, with Phase 1 spend included in existing 2026 guidance.

headline: NORTHERN STAR SURGES 12% on ASX After Pogo Mine Drill Results Beat Analyst Expectations
snippet: Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST) led the ASX 200 with a 12.4% gain on June 2, closing at a 52-week high after reporting high-grade gold intercepts from its Pogo mine in Alaska and its Australian operations that exceeded analyst projections. The result reinforces Northern Star as one of the strongest-performing large-cap gold producers on the ASX in 2026.

headline: COPPER AT $6.56/LB: Chile's April Output Falls 13.8% — Worst April in Over Two Decades
snippet: Chile's copper production dropped 13.8% year-on-year to 399,954 tonnes in April—the worst April figure in more than 20 years—as low ore grades and a tough comparison base weighed on output. With Grasberg also running below capacity, COMEX copper has climbed to $6.56/lb on June 2 (up 35% year-on-year), driven by AI data-center build-out and electrification demand absorbing a supply-constrained market.

headline: ECB CONFIRMS Gold Has Overtaken US Treasuries as World's Top Reserve Asset — First Time Since 1996
snippet: The European Central Bank confirmed that gold now accounts for 27% of global reserve assets—seven percentage points above year-ago levels—overtaking US Treasuries at 22% for the first time since the Bretton Woods era ended. Sustained buying by China, Poland, Turkey, and India drove the shift; central banks collectively hold more than 36,000 tonnes of gold, approaching Bretton Woods-era levels.

headline: HONG KONG Beats Switzerland as World's Biggest Wealth Hub, Powered by July Gold Clearing House Launch
snippet: Hong Kong has surpassed Switzerland as the world's largest cross-border wealth hub per BCG's 2026 Global Wealth Report, driven by its strategic push into gold trading. A new Hong Kong gold-clearing system launches in July, with plans to expand storage capacity tenfold to over 2,000 tonnes. More than half of global gold coin and bar demand now originates from China and India—a structural shift in where gold capital flows.
